question: Two tones sound together on every beat; now and then one arrives early. Which one do tapping hands correct for more?
answer: The lower tone. Michael Hove and colleagues found early low tones drew larger brain responses and larger tapping corrections than early high ones. A model of the inner ear traced the edge to the ear itself. It may be why bass and kick drum, not the melody, lay down the beat.
move: Ask which channel carries the timing before trusting the one that carries the tune.
trap: The higher tone, since melodies sit high and draw the attention.
reference: Hove, Marie, Bruce & Trainor, Superior time perception for lower musical pitch explains why bass-ranged instruments lay down musical rhythms, PNAS, 2014
